earlier_scan.note: New Caledonia; only Haudricourt 1971 classification comment; no grammar or phonology located.

sources.citation: Osumi, Midori. 1995. Tinrin grammar (New Caledonia). PhD thesis, ANU (published as Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 25). hdl:1885/132714
sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE ONLY (Tinrin, tiri1258), not Neku: sec. 2.4 p. 25 'The stress falls generally on the first syllable in a multisyllabic word'; stressed syllable higher pitch. The grammar never mentions Neku (grep neku/Ouaoué/Bourail = 0 hits), so it cannot be used for neku1237.

sources.citation: Osumi, Midori. 2011. Evaluation constructions in Tinrin and Neku (New Caledonia): survey with typological overview. Ronshu (Tokyo Woman's Christian University) 61(2): 139-178.
sources.note: Nothing. Footnote 2 says Neku data were collected in Ouaoué 2000-2009 and 'the research on Neku is still underway'; footnote 3 gives orthography (vowels, consonants) only, no stress.

sources.citation: 大角翠 (Osumi, Midori). 2009. ティンリン語、ネク語に見られる動詞類別接頭辞の概念体系とイベント分類的機能 [Semantic perspectives and event-classifying functions of verbal prefixes in Tinrin & Neku]. 東京女子大学比較文化研究所紀要 70: 1-17.
sources.note: Nothing; intro only notes Neku is spoken at Ouaoué and Moméa (central Grande Terre), 221 speakers (1996).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page neku1237; KAKEN project reports 12039240, 16520261, 19520366, 23520525 (PI Osumi); Académie des Langues Kanak page 'Neku'; Lexibank/ABVD Neku wordlist; en.wikipedia stub
sources.note: Nothing on stress. ALK: 125 speakers over 14 (ISEE 2009), plant-name corpus only. KAKEN reports: Neku grammar and dictionary 'ongoing', no previous written records; a Neku picture book (2013) exists.
